title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 309-310): Grothendieck is rewriting the classical Legendre relation between elliptic curves and P^1 minus 4 points purely in terms of 'groupes a lacets', the discrete or profinite fundamental groups of type (g,nu) with their inertia (cusp) data. Earlier this was done via Teichmueller groups (his eq. (55)). Here he wants to do it directly with pi_{0,3}/pi_{0,4} and pi_{1,1}.

Step 1. Let pi' be a loop group of type (1,1). Topologically this is pi_1 of a once-punctured torus E\{0}: free of rank 2, with a distinguished inertia class. The previous page notes that Autext(pi') = Out(pi') contains a canonical element of order 2, written (-1)_{pi'}. It is the elliptic involution: it acts as -1 on the abelianization and preserves orientation.

Step 2. So pi' carries an outer action of G = Z/2Z. Since pi' has trivial center, an outer action determines a canonical extension (58): 1 -> pi' -> E -> Z/2Z -> 1. Concretely, E is the preimage of <(-1)> in Aut(pi').

Step 3. The topological model is E ~ U x U (U the circle group) with x -> -x. This tells us there are exactly three pi'-conjugacy classes of splittings of (58). They correspond to the three fixed points of x -> -x on E\{0}, i.e. the three nonzero 2-torsion points.
- Check in the discrete case: E is the orbifold fundamental group of (E\{0})/+-1. That orbifold is a sphere with one puncture and three cone points of order 2, so E ~ Z/2 * Z/2 * Z/2.
- Splittings are subgroups of order 2 not contained in pi'. Their E-conjugacy and pi'-conjugacy coincide, because the splitting element centralizes itself. Free products have exactly three conjugacy classes of involutions here.

Step 4. He invokes a theory of '"fourgons ... simultanes"' for finite groups of outer operators on loop groups. This theory is unwritten; he says that for now there are only conjectural statements, even in the discrete case. Recall that in La Longue Marche the 'fourgon' is the extension pi_{g,nu+1} over pi_{g,nu} obtained by adding a puncture, i.e. point-pushing / Birman. The simultaneous, equivariant version would let one algebraically 'puncture' at the G-fixed-point classes, i.e. at the splitting classes.

Step 5 (next page). The theory yields canonically a loop group tilde-pi' of type (1,4) = pi_1(E \ E[2]). It comes with:
- an outer G-action;
- a G-stable 3-element subset J of the 4 cusps;
- an isomorphism (59), compatible with G, between pi' and the group obtained by 'filling the holes in J'.
Here G acts freely on E \ E[2]. The quotient is P^1 minus 4 points, so the extension (60) of Z/2 by tilde-pi' is pi_{0,4}. This is the group-theoretic Legendre correspondence pi_{1,1} <-> pi_{0,4}.

The page thus serves a purely combinatorial / anabelian derivation of Legendre's equivalence. It amounts to an algebraic 'cuspidalization of the 2-torsion points' driven by the elliptic involution.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The count of three splitting classes is correct in the discrete case, since E = Z/2*Z/2*Z/2.

In the profinite case Grothendieck appeals only to the 'topological model'. The profinite statement is true but needs an extra input: the profinite completion is the free profinite product of three Z/2, and finite subgroups of free profinite products are conjugate into factors (Herfort-Ribes, 1985). The page does not justify this step.
The 'fourgons simultanes' theory is explicitly stated to be unwritten and conjectural, so the construction on the next page depends on unproved statements (as he acknowledges).

ideas.what: The elliptic involution as a canonical order-2 element of Out(pi_{1,1}), and the canonical extension of Z/2 by pi' it defines.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group of the quotient of the once-punctured torus by -1; the hyperelliptic involution in Out(F_2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Nielsen; Fricke-Klein); standard in genus-one GT/anabelian work (Nakamura, Lochak-Schneps)
ideas.where_published: Not as such; Esquisse mentions the (1,1) vs (0,4) relation only in passing

ideas.what: Conjugacy classes of splittings of the extension correspond bijectively to fixed points of the involution (three 2-torsion points).
ideas.modern_name: Fixed points <-> conjugacy classes of sections/finite subgroups (Nielsen fixed-point classes; profinite version via Herfort-Ribes; 'section conjecture' for finite group actions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discrete: classical. Profinite: Herfort-Ribes (1985), Zalesskii and others on torsion in profinite completions of Fuchsian groups

ideas.what: Theory of 'fourgons simultanes' for finite groups of outer operators on loop groups: algebraically puncturing a surface group at the fixed-point classes of a finite outer action, producing pi_{g,nu+k} with compatible cusp data.
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant point-pushing / orbifold Birman sequence; group-theoretic cuspidalization (Mochizuki's cuspidalization, especially 'elliptic cuspidalization' of torsion points; Hoshi-Mochizuki combinatorial cuspidalization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: S. Mochizuki (2007 absolute anabelian cuspidalizations; etale theta / IUT elliptic cuspidalization); Hoshi-Mochizuki (2009-)
ideas.where_published: 'Fourgons' appear in La Longue Marche, but not this simultaneous equivariant version

ideas.what: Group-theoretic Legendre equivalence: pi_{0,4} as the extension of Z/2 by pi_1(E minus E[2]), with E[2]\{0} recovered from involution sections.
ideas.modern_name: Legendre level-2 correspondence M_{0,4} vs M_{1,1}[2] at the level of fundamental groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; used by Nakamura and Lochak-Schneps-Nakamura for the genus-one GT action

missed.claim: Grothendieck's programme here anticipates Mochizuki's 'elliptic cuspidalization'. That is the group-theoretic reconstruction of pi_1(E minus torsion points) from pi_1(E\{0}) together with an outer action (here the ±1 symmetry), with sections of the extension serving as surrogate torsion points. He proposes a general 'fourgons simultanes' theory for arbitrary finite groups of outer automorphisms of loop groups, which he says is unwritten even in the discrete case.
missed.quote: La théorie des "fourgons ... simultanés", relatif à une situation d'un groupe fini d'opérateurs extérieurs dans des groupes à lacets (théorie qui n'a vraiment été écrite — il y a pour le moment des énoncés conjecturaux)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A general equivariant cuspidalization theorem would be a clean statement in combinatorial anabelian geometry and profinite surface-group theory. Given a finite group of outer automorphisms of pi_{g,nu}, it would canonically produce the loop group with fixed points punctured, plus filling-in isomorphisms. Mochizuki and Hoshi-Mochizuki cover special cases, but Grothendieck's general formulation does not appear to be credited.

missed.claim: He asserts, without proof, that splitting classes correspond exactly to fixed points for finite outer actions on loop groups. The profinite case needs results such as Herfort-Ribes (finite subgroups of free profinite products) or profinite Nielsen-realization-type statements. The general (g,nu), arbitrary finite G version is left conjectural.
missed.quote: Le modèle topologique nous apprend qu'il y a exactement trois classes de π'-conjugaison de scindages
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the profinite analogue of the correspondence between fixed points and conjugacy classes of sections for finite groups acting on curves, used in Galois-theoretic Teichmüller theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The concrete mathematics is classical: the Legendre correspondence and three classes of involutions. The mildly notable part is Grothendieck's explicit sketch of an unwritten, conjectural 'fourgons simultanés' theory of equivariant group-theoretic cuspidalization at fixed points. It foreshadows Mochizuki-style cuspidalization, but it is only announced, not developed.
transcription_corrections: 'U×U' is correct (circle group U), i.e. E ≃ U×U.
The phrase transcribed 'fourgons de lacs simultanés' is uncertain. The middle word is illegible; it may be 'fourgons de [bouchage?] simultanés' or similar.

The sentence reads roughly 'théorie qui n'a vraiment été écrite [even] dans le cas discret — il y a pour le moment des énoncés conjecturaux'. The insertion is likely 'n'a même pas été écrite dans le cas discret'.
The oblique margin note is roughly 'mais ici on se borne à des [fourgons] ... des fourgons [catégoriques?]... 2 fois'. It is largely illegible.
